title: On-demand slab lifecycle and KV seed heuristics for faster Dedicated cold-starts
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets serving high-throughput tenants experience long cold-start tails when nodes are (re)provisioned or when tenant traffic ramps. Current warm-pool approaches pre-load large weight snapshots and opportunistically prime KV caches, but we lack a tenant-aware slab lifecycle that balances memory residency, I/O throughput guarantees, and autoscaler signals. This ticket defines an on-demand slab lifecycle plus KV seed heuristics to reduce 95/99th startup latency while preserving throughput SLAs and cost targets.

Goals:
- Reduce median cold-start token latency by >= 30% and 95th by >= 50% for Dedicated fleets for typical 2–8k token workloads.
- Maintain throughput guarantees for reserved capacity during aggressive prewarming and avoid cross-tenant eviction storms.
- Integrate with autoscaler to perform progressive slab admission tied to target QPS and headroom thresholds.
- Provide observable metrics and runbook to rollback/adjust heuristics quickly.

Constraints/Assumptions:
- Weight streaming bandwidth per node is bounded by NIC/GPU bus; prewarming should not starve inference or background replication traffic.
- Some tenant models have >40GB of weights; slab granularity should support partial residency.
- KV priming should be idempotent and cost-aware (avoid aggressive priming for rare prefixes).

Design sketch:
1) Slab Lifecycle: treat model parameters as ordered slabs with hotness metadata (recent traffic, forecasted demand). Nodes maintain a compact SlabState with residency status {resident,prefetching,staged}. Admission is driven by an AdmissionScore combining tenant priority, forecasted QPS, and node headroom.
2) On-demand streaming: support throttled slab streaming with backpressure signals to avoid saturating interconnects. Streaming prioritizes slabs needed for typical context/window used by the tenant (first M layers + attention KV heavy slabs).
3) KV seed heuristics: maintain per-tenant prefix histogram (sampled) and a lightweight KV-Priming budget. When slab residency reaches resident, background priming probes top-K prefixes (configurable) using small synthetic requests routed to the same node to populate KV cache without counting against customer billing metrics.
4) Autoscaler integration: the node-level controller exposes a WarmnessScore; autoscaler uses WarmnessScore + pending requests to decide whether to bring new nodes up or trigger proactive prewarming on spare nodes.
5) Admission policies and throttles: global rate limit for simultaneous slab streams per rack + per-tenant soft quota to prevent noisy tenants from blocking others.

Deliverables:
- Controller changes (admission scoring, slab state machine).
- Streaming and backpressure primitives in weight-loader runtime.
- KV priming worker and budget controller.
- Console dashboards and SLO alerts for warm metric regressions.

Success metrics:
- Cold-start 95th token latency for Dedicated down by >=50% in canary.
- No more than 5% degradation of steady-state throughput for other tenants during warm streaming.
- WarmnessScore correlates with decreased tail latency (observable in dashboards).
acceptance_criteria: Canary rollout to a single Dedicated fleet region shows >=50% reduction in 95th cold-start latency for target models (runbook: compare pre/post with identical traffic replay)
WarmnessScore produced by controller is exported as a metric and matches expected values for resident/prefetching/staged states
KV priming worker successfully populates local KV cache for the top-50 prefixes without causing request billing or affecting production inference QPS
Streaming rate limits and per-tenant quotas prevent noisy-tenant inhibition in synthetic stress tests (no tenant sees >10% increase in inference latency during warming windows)
Monitoring dashboards and automated alerts (SLO breach and warm-failure) are in place in Console and tested by injection
implementation_plan: Week 1: Implement SlabState machine and AdmissionScore proto + unit tests
Week 2: Add throttled slab-streaming path in weight-loader; implement node-level backpressure channels
Week 3: Implement KV priming worker and budget controller with synthetic probe harness
Week 4: Integrate WarmnessScore into autoscaler signals and add simulation tests to validate scaling decisions
Week 5: Canary on dedicated-fleet-east-2 (low risk tenant set), collect metrics and iterate heuristics
Week 6: Expand rollout to additional fleets and finalize dashboarding and runbook
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics: slab_stream_bytes, slab_stream_rate, slab_prefetch_count, warmness_score, kv_probe_success_rate, kv_probe_latency
Dashboards: per-fleet warmness heatmap, cold-start latency trends (p50/p95/p99), cross-tenant impact panel
Alerts: warm_failure_rate > 1% over 5m, slab_stream_saturation per-rack > 80%, kv_probe_error_rate > 0.5%
Runbook: automated rollback toggle to disable prewarming across fleet and fail open to default admission policy
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive prewarming saturates interconnect and reduces steady throughput. Mitigation: global/rack throttles + streaming backpressure + canary gradients.
Risk: KV priming probes inflate request metrics or bill customers. Mitigation: synthetic probes flagged internal and excluded from billing/quotas; sample-based priming budget tied to tenant SLA tier.
Risk: Prediction-based admission misallocates memory leading to eviction storms. Mitigation: conservative defaults, soft quotas per-tenant, and emergency eviction circuit breaker.
Risk: Complexity in autoscaler coupling introduces oscillations. Mitigation: introduce damping (cooldown windows) and test in simulator with real traffic traces.
Risk: Security/privacy concerns with sampled prefixes. Mitigation: only collect hashed prefix histograms and respect PII redaction policies (security review if changed).
